translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Whether the ghosts are real or the governess’s fantasy is never resolved in the Vietnamese: hedges (‘I suppose’, ‘as it were’) are kept, and broken-off lines (for example ‘I might.’) stay broken off.
decisions.rationale: The story’s power is that both readings remain open.

decisions.decision: James’s long periodic sentences are broken at natural junctures and recast in Vietnamese syntax rather than kept word for word; translationese was the main fault of the first drafts.
decisions.rationale: Naturalness was the weakest sub-score through five review rounds.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: Five majors in units 44, 116, 135, 136 and 180 (calqued ‘face the music’, a garbled clause, ‘turned real’, a wrong address form and ‘inconsequence’) were corrected.
‘on this’ rendered ‘before this’ (unit 377), ‘girded her loins’ rendered as an austerity idiom (650) and ‘with nothing on’ rendered ‘naked’ (607) were corrected.
‘sân thượng’ used for both the tower and the ground-level terrace (137, 143–144), and the returned question ‘Do you?’ (742), were corrected.
The broken-off line ‘I might.’ had been completed with an added phrase; it is left broken off. ‘incapacity’ (339) and a double negative that flipped a hedge (231) were also corrected.
Calqued syntax and pronoun slips (governess ‘bà’, Quint and Jessel forms) were recast over several rounds.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.rationale: Douglas’s idiom that gives the tale its title; one wording wherever it recurs.

glossary.source_term: the governess / my employer / the children
glossary.draft_rendering: cô gia sư (tôi) / ngài chủ nhà / hai học trò nhỏ
glossary.rationale: Fixed forms of address through the tale, with the governess always ‘tôi/cô’ in her own narration.

glossary.draft_rendering: Peter Quint (hắn/gã) / cô Jessel (bà ta/cô ấy)
glossary.rationale: Names kept; the pronouns separate the governess’s voice from Mrs. Grose’s.
One word family for the apparitions, avoiding terms that fix them as real or imagined.

witness_decision: Selected Project Gutenberg #209, an electronic transcription of Henry James’s The Turn of the Screw as published in the collection The Two Magics (New York: Macmillan, 1898); the story first appeared in Collier’s Weekly (27 January – 16 April 1898). The Gutenberg page does not name the exact printing and the text was not collated.

unresolved_questions.explanation: A few long periods remain heavier than natural Vietnamese prose would have them.

title_review.rationale: The Vietnamese title ‘Một vòng ốc nữa’ is this edition’s own rendering of the idiom ‘another turn of the screw’; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The frame: Christmas Eve around the fire.
